description:
A Go compiler, code editor and learning workspace for iPhone and iPad. Build, run, test, vet and format on your device with the bundled Go 1.27.1 toolchain, even offline.

BUILD REAL PROJECTS
• Edit Go and go.mod with highlighting, completion and keyboard shortcuts.
• Follow diagnostics to source lines and inspect per-case test results.
• Import public GitHub repositories, folders from Files or exported archives.
• Navigate nested folders and dependencies; organize projects with tags, favorites and file-name search.
• Download compatible pure-Go modules through the official Go proxy and checksum database. Vendored sources build offline.
• Keep working during downloads, inspect failures and retry from Output. Clear downloaded packages without deleting your source.

LEARN GO
• Follow 169 teaching lessons in 21 units, plus 22 prediction challenges: core Go, structs, collections, interfaces, errors, modules, generics, concurrency and the standard library.
• Read 122 worked lessons, including 19 architecture and eight clean-code lessons, all 23 classic design patterns and six concurrent Go patterns. Compare architecture suitability for tools, domain-rich apps and services with editorial ratings.
• Study Bash, Git, curl, Linux services, Docker, Compose, Podman and Kubernetes with actual commands, probes, scaling and rollback examples.
• Explore twelve MongoDB/Redis readings: shared clients, indexes, atomicity, transactions, cursors, caching, streams and load.
• Packages, modules and tooling now has fourteen teaching lessons covering version graphs, checksums, workspaces, vendor/embed, parallel tests, benchmarks, profiles, build budgets and resource ownership.
• Use 69 original visual guides, 80 design diagrams, practical notes and primary references. Expand highlighted code to full screen.
• Match concepts in Review and work on saved mistakes with three-answer questions and explanations. Progress survives reopening.

PREPARE FOR INTERVIEWS
• Open the separate Interview area: 88 worked guides across 12 topics, from Junior to Staff / expert.
• Explain an answer, compare the reasoning, spot a common trap, solve a worked exercise and tackle a follow-up. Save personal self-assessment separately from lesson completion.
• Cover language/runtime, concurrency, architecture, HTTP/SQL, testing, modules, MongoDB, Redis, Docker/Kubernetes and Go workflows with Claude Code, Codex and Cursor.
• Step through eight algorithms with 24 input scenarios: binary search, two sum, sliding window, BFS, Dijkstra, top-K, merge and dynamic programming. Inspect state changes and read the Go implementations and complexity.

MADE FOR YOUR SCREEN
Collapsible Files, code and results adapt to iPhone and iPad. Supported iPhone Duo layouts respond to display and posture, including code above the fold with keyboard or tools below. Transparent lower scroll edges and extra scroll room keep final lines reachable without inserting source lines. Choose theme, text size, keep-awake during builds and downloads, and Face ID or passcode locking.

PRIVACY AND LIMITS
One paid download. No subscription, app account, analytics or advertising trackers. Projects and progress stay local; a chosen Files/iCloud library follows your provider. Imports, package downloads and external links use the network.

Compiled Go runs in a bounded WebAssembly/WASI sandbox: no guest network, cgo or arbitrary shell. Terminal commands are app-supported. Database, shell, deployment and coding-agent guides teach your own development environment; they do not connect the app to AI providers or install services. WebKit previews may load project-linked remote resources.

promotionalText: Learn Go and prepare for interviews: 88 worked guides, eight interactive algorithm labs, plus expanded MongoDB, Redis and production-tooling lessons.

reviewNotes:
GopherForge 1.1.4 build 39. No account or demo credentials required.

Learn now has Course and Interview segments. Interview provides 88 worked guides across 12 topics and four difficulty levels (Junior through Staff / expert). It is available immediately without completion gates. Each guide includes answer reasoning, a common trap, a worked exercise and solution, a follow-up and primary sources. Self-assessment is stored locally and does not claim compiler verification or an interview score.

In Interview > Algorithm demonstrations, open Binary search. Choose Duplicates, Empty or Beyond end, then use Next step, Back and Reset. Eight algorithms have 24 preset scenarios and 111 computed states. These are deterministic educational traces shared byte-for-byte with the website, not arbitrary remote execution. Published Go implementations are included. AI-provider guides are educational text with official links; there is no AI login, API integration or AI-generated app content at runtime.

Course contains 169 teaching lessons in 21 units, 122 readings and 22 prediction challenges. Around Go: MongoDB and Redis has twelve new readings. Packages, modules and tooling has twelve additional readings after its original two teaching exercises. Every new reading has a flow diagram, worked snippets, references, a matching pair and a three-choice review question. Existing IDs and progress remain stable.

Database, shell and deployment examples are educational text for a native development environment. They do not install databases, add cgo/arbitrary shell/network sockets or alter module archive budgets in the app's WebAssembly/WASI sandbox. Compilation remains local with bundled Go 1.27.1. Web previews may load project-linked remote resources.

The native editor and lesson scroll view hide the lower edge backdrop around floating controls. End space belongs to scrolling content, never source text. Embedded code still scrolls with its lesson; full-screen code scrolls independently. Keyboard/hinge routing is preserved.

To verify the compiler, Projects > Create new project > Worker pool, then Build > Run. Package with tests shows per-case results. No native analytics, advertising, account, subscription or in-app purchase was added. Website progress is separate from native progress. One paid app download; web lessons and interview guides are free.

The workspace now waits for its initial project to load before exposing pane controls. This prevents the initial project-generation reset from undoing an early Terminal tap. Opening failures show a project-unavailable state.
